references.authors: Stanstrup J, Neumann S, Vrhovšek U
references.title: PredRet: Prediction of Retention Time by Direct Mapping between Multiple Chromatographic Systems
references.verification: Crossref /works record (title match) and PubMed PMID 26289378 abstract retrieved this session; methods read from the open-access PDF (openpub.fmach.it).
references.category: Calibrant/overlap-based projection between chromatographic systems
references.problem: Share experimental RTs across labs and chromatographic systems (CSs) so that RT can help discriminate isomers in untargeted LC-MS.
references.data: Community-uploaded experimental RT database (predret.org) of several RP and HILIC CSs, with up to about 400 predicted RTs per CS at publication.
references.method: Pairwise robust, monotonically constrained GAMs (mgcv, sigmoid-weighted penalized constrained least squares) fitted on compounds measured on both CSs, with at least 10 shared compounds required.
references.uncertainty_method: Bootstrap (1000 resamples) 99% prediction intervals; predictions whose PI is wider than 2 min or 20% of RT are discarded, and the authors call the PIs anticonservative.
references.transfer_setting: Experimental-to-experimental projection between pairs of CSs of the same chromatography type; the query compound must already have a measured RT in a source CS.
references.main_results: Median prediction error 0.01-0.28 min and median PI width 0.08-1.86 min across CSs.
references.code_available: Yes: R package for querying the database (github.com/stanstrup/PredRet) and web service predret.org, as stated in the paper.
references.limitations: Cannot predict compounds never measured on an overlapping system, and its PIs have no coverage guarantee; the authors advise against using them as strict exclusion filters.
references.relevance_to_study: Canonical monotone calibrant-mapping baseline and the archetype of heuristic (bootstrap) RT intervals that our jackknife+ conformal windows are meant to replace with guaranteed coverage.

references.authors: Abate-Pella D, Freund DM, Ma Y, Simón-Manso Y, Hollender J, Broeckling CD, Huhman DV, Krokhin OV, Stoll DR, Hegeman AD, Kind T, Fiehn O, Schymanski EL, Prenni JE, Sumner LW, Boswell PG
references.title: Retention projection enables accurate calculation of liquid chromatographic retention times across labs and methods
references.verification: PubMed PMID 26292625 (title match) and author-manuscript full text PMC4556278 retrieved this session.
references.category: Physics-based cross-lab RT transfer using calibration standards
references.problem: Calculate gradient RTs across laboratories and methods more reliably than linear retention indices (LRIs).
references.data: Eight-lab study with one test mixture (20 instrument-calibration standards plus 19 test compounds) on Eclipse Plus C18 columns, using isocratic k-vs-phi data from a reference lab.
references.method: Retention projection from isocratic k-vs-phi relationships, combined with back-calculation of each lab's effective gradient and dead-time profiles from the co-injected calibration standards.
references.uncertainty_method: None beyond reported error ranges (for example ±0.27 to ±0.99 s for method 1); no prediction intervals.
references.transfer_setting: Same stationary and mobile phase, transferred across instruments, gradients and flow rates using calibration standards run on the target system.
references.main_results: For uncharged compounds, projections were on average 22-fold more accurate than LRIs under lab-chosen gradients and 2-fold more accurate under nominally identical conditions.
references.code_available: Yes: open-source Java software (retentionprediction.org/hplc/development) and an open k-vs-phi database.
references.limitations: Every compound needs measured isocratic k-vs-phi relationships on the same column chemistry, which the authors call a major drawback; charged compounds were less accurate because of column ageing.
references.relevance_to_study: Mechanistic calibrant-based transfer baseline showing that calibrant runs can absorb instrument-level differences, but it cannot cover novel structures as an ML base score can.

references.authors: Bach E, Szedmak S, Brouard C, Böcker S, Rousu J
references.title: Liquid-chromatography retention order prediction for metabolite identification
references.verification: PubMed PMID 30423079 record and abstract retrieved by DOI this session (title match).
references.category: Retention-order (pairwise ranking) learning across LC systems
references.problem: Use LC information for metabolite identification even though absolute RTs do not transfer between systems.
references.data: Heterogeneous public RT datasets from different LC systems and configurations, pooled without tedious pre-processing.
references.method: Ranking SVM learning a retention-order score from molecular representations, then combined with MS/MS scores over a whole LC-MS/MS run.
references.uncertainty_method: None (order scores only).
references.transfer_setting: Train on pooled multi-system data and predict elution order, not times, on other systems; chromatographic conditions are not encoded.
references.main_results: Showed that retention order is much better conserved between instruments than RT, and that combining order with MS/MS scores improves identification.
references.code_available: Yes: version.aalto.fi/gitlab/bache1/retention_order_prediction (stated in abstract).
references.limitations: Gives no absolute RTs or tolerance windows and cannot represent condition-specific changes in elution order.
references.relevance_to_study: Direct conceptual precursor of our pairwise-ranking retention-order base score; we add condition-aware multi-system training on RepoRT, calibrant mapping and calibrated windows.

references.authors: Bouwmeester R, Martens L, Degroeve S
references.title: Comprehensive and Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Small Molecule LC Retention Time Prediction
references.verification: Crossref record (title match; bioRxiv preprint relation) and PubMed PMID 30702864 abstract retrieved this session; repository README checked.
references.category: Single-system ML RT prediction benchmark
references.problem: Determine which ML algorithms and feature sets work best for small-molecule LC RT prediction.
references.data: 36 distinct metabolomics RT datasets (raw data from the Aicheler et al. set, MoNA and PredRet) with two feature sets.
references.method: Systematic comparison of seven machine-learning algorithms plus blending of model types.
references.uncertainty_method: None reported (point predictions).
references.transfer_setting: Setup-specific models trained and tested within each dataset; no cross-system transfer.
references.main_results: No single algorithm was best on all datasets, and blending models reduced errors on outliers.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/RobbinBouwmeester/tRPredictionOverview (data, scripts, models).
references.limitations: Needs substantial training data from the target system and gives only point predictions.
references.relevance_to_study: Shows that base-model accuracy depends on the dataset, which motivates model-agnostic calibrated windows; it is also a source of benchmark datasets.

references.authors: Domingo-Almenara X, Guijas C, Billings E, Montenegro-Burke JR, Uritboonthai W, Aisporna AE, Chen E, Benton HP, Siuzdak G
references.title: The METLIN small molecule dataset for machine learning-based retention time prediction
references.verification: Crossref and PubMed PMID 31862874 records plus full text PMC6925099 retrieved this session.
references.category: Large single-system RT dataset with DL model and predicted-to-experimental projection
references.problem: RT prediction accuracy is limited by the small size of experimental datasets.
references.data: SMRT: 80,038 small molecules measured on one RP HPLC-MS method (Zorbax Extend-C18), with projection tests on PredRet CMs using HMDB/KEGG candidates.
references.method: Fingerprint-based deep-learning regressor; predicted RTs were projected to other CMs by a fourth-order polynomial fitted on 50 randomly selected known molecules.
references.uncertainty_method: None; candidate-filter RT thresholds were chosen post hoc from ROC curves (relative error 10-27.5%).
references.transfer_setting: Predicted-to-experimental projection to four external PredRet CMs (FEM_long, LIFE_old, RIKEN, FEM_orbitrap_plasma).
references.main_results: Median relative and absolute errors were 4.6% and 35 s, with the correct identity in the top 3 in up to 70% of cases, yet ROC-tuned thresholds discarded 21-41% of correct identities.
references.code_available: Yes: data and R scripts on Figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.8038913).
references.limitations: The authors concluded that predicted-experimental RT filtering is not robust, because the threshold varied strongly with the random projection subset; elution order is not conserved across HILIC methods.
references.relevance_to_study: Main pretraining resource, and the clearest documentation that heuristic ROC-tuned windows lose many true identities, which is our core motivation.

references.authors: Bonini P, Kind T, Tsugawa H, Barupal DK, Fiehn O
references.title: Retip: Retention Time Prediction for Compound Annotation in Untargeted Metabolomics
references.verification: Crossref and PubMed PMID 32390414 records plus full text PMC8715951 retrieved this session.
references.category: Single-system ML RT tool integrated into annotation software
references.problem: Raise confidence in untargeted LC-MS/MS annotations by predicting RT from structure.
references.data: Fiehn HILIC set (about 970-981 metabolites, BEH Amide) and RIKEN PlaSMA RPLC set (852 specialized metabolites).
references.method: R package with random forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM and Keras on CDK descriptors, with export of predictions to MS-DIAL and MS-FINDER.
references.uncertainty_method: Fixed ±1 min RT windows (about the MAE) for candidate exclusion; no interval model.
references.transfer_setting: None; users retrain on their own chromatographic method.
references.main_results: Keras MAE was 0.78 min (HILIC) and 0.57 min (RPLC), and ±1 min filtering excluded 68% of candidate structures in plasma HILIC data.
references.code_available: Yes: R package (retip.app, GitHub).
references.limitations: ±1 min windows held only 87% (RP) and 65% (HILIC) of test true positives and excluded about 25% of true positives overall, with no per-compound adaptation.
references.relevance_to_study: Representative fixed-minute window heuristic that our conformal windows are benchmarked against on coverage versus decoy elimination, for both RP and HILIC.

references.authors: Bouwmeester R, Martens L, Degroeve S
references.title: Generalized Calibration Across Liquid Chromatography Setups for Generic Prediction of Small-Molecule Retention Times
references.verification: PubMed PMID 32281370 abstract and Crossref record of the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2020.01.14.905844) retrieved this session; layer details from the bioRxiv full text via WebFetch.
references.category: Calibration of predicted RTs across LC setups
references.problem: Avoid fitting a new RT model for each setup by mapping models between experimental setups.
references.data: Many public RT datasets (setups); preprint learning curves use 20-100 calibration analytes from the target setup.
references.method: Three layers: setup-specific regressors, GAM (mgcv) calibration of each model's predictions to target RTs, and an elastic-net combination of the calibrated predictions.
references.uncertainty_method: None for individual predictions (the preprint shows only an SD band for the GAM fit).
references.transfer_setting: Transfer of models trained on other setups to a target setup using a modest set of calibration analytes.
references.main_results: Generalized calibration gave substantially higher elution-peak prediction accuracy than setup-specific models.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/compomics/CALLC.
references.limitations: Point predictions only; accuracy depends on the number and coverage of calibrants, and tolerances are not coverage-controlled.
references.relevance_to_study: Closest ML precursor of our 'project a public model, then map with calibrants' stage, but it provides no calibrated windows.

references.authors: Yang Q, Ji H, Lu H, Zhang Z
references.title: Prediction of Liquid Chromatographic Retention Time with Graph Neural Networks to Assist in Small Molecule Identification
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 33406817 abstract retrieved this session; GitHub README checked.
references.category: Single-system GNN RT prediction with transfer learning
references.problem: Improve RT prediction accuracy for structure identification without hand-crafted descriptors.
references.data: METLIN SMRT (RP) for training, with transfer to other datasets of the same chromatography type.
references.method: End-to-end graph neural network on molecular graphs, compared with RF, Bayesian ridge, CNN and DLM baselines, plus fine-tuning for transfer.
references.uncertainty_method: None.
references.transfer_setting: Pretrain on SMRT, then fine-tune on target datasets of the same chromatography type (requires target training data).
references.main_results: Mean and median relative errors of 4.9% and 3.2% on SMRT, the best among the compared models.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/Qiong-Yang/GNN-RT (preprocess, train and transfer-learning scripts).
references.limitations: Transfer needs fine-tuning data from each target system, and it offers neither uncertainty nor a calibrant-only protocol.
references.relevance_to_study: Representative pretrain/fine-tune paradigm that cannot operate with only n≈10-50 calibrants.

references.authors: Aalizadeh R, Alygizakis NA, Schymanski EL, Krauss M, Schulze T, Ibáñez M, McEachran AD, Chao A, Williams AJ, Gago-Ferrero P, Covaci A, Moschet C, Young TM, Hollender J, Slobodnik J, Thomaidis NS
references.title: Development and Application of Liquid Chromatographic Retention Time Indices in HRMS-Based Suspect and Nontarget Screening
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 34382770 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
references.category: Calibrant-based RT index harmonisation for NTS
references.problem: Make LC RTs comparable between laboratories as supporting evidence in HRMS suspect and nontarget screening.
references.data: Two sets of 18 calibrants (ESI+ and ESI−) chosen from 2,123 compounds, with external validation on other instruments and LC conditions coordinated by NORMAN.
references.method: Unified retention time index (RTI, 1-1000) calibrated on the calibrant elution pattern, plus QSRR models that predict RTI.
references.uncertainty_method: QSRR applicability domains flag substances whose predictions should be treated with caution; no calibrated intervals.
references.transfer_setting: Cross-lab transfer of RP RTs through the calibrant-based RTI.
references.main_results: The RTI system was validated externally and used to remove false-positive annotations in two NTS examples (online at rti.chem.uoa.gr).
references.code_available: Web tool rti.chem.uoa.gr; source code not stated in the abstract.
references.limitations: Applicability-domain flags are qualitative; a later study (Malm & Kruve 2025) found RTIs sensitive to nonlinear gradient programs.
references.relevance_to_study: NTS standard for calibrant-based harmonisation; our calibrant mapping with conformal windows adds quantitative, coverage-controlled tolerances in the same workflow.

references.authors: García CA, Gil-de-la-Fuente A, Barbas C, Otero A
references.title: Probabilistic metabolite annotation using retention time prediction and meta-learned projections
references.verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 35672784 and full text PMC9172150 retrieved this session.
references.category: Few-calibrant probabilistic projection with meta-learning across chromatographic methods
references.problem: Project SMRT-trained RT predictions to a lab's chromatographic method from very few identified molecules while quantifying uncertainty.
references.data: SMRT (80,038 RTs) for base models; PredRet CMs as meta-tasks, with FEM long, FEM orbitrap plasma, LIFE old and RIKEN as targets.
references.method: Regularized DNN base predictor plus a Gaussian-process projection whose prior (mean and kernel) is meta-learned on other CMs by minimizing a leave-one-out predictive loss.
references.uncertainty_method: GP posterior predictive 95% intervals, scored with the interval score; z-scores rank candidates.
references.transfer_setting: Leave-one-CM-out with 10-50 stratified calibrants from the target CM.
references.main_results: On SMRT the DNN reached MAE 39.2 s and MedAE 17.2 s; the meta-learned GP had the best scaled interval score in 3 of 4 CMs, and the correct molecule was in the top 3 in 68% (10 calibrants) to 70% (50 calibrants) of queries.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/constantino-garcia/cmmrt.
references.limitations: Gaussian, model-based intervals without finite-sample coverage guarantees, tested on only four target CMs; the 1-D GP variance depends on the base predicted RT, not on molecule-level novelty.
references.relevance_to_study: Closest prior idea to our meta-learning across systems for few-calibrant intervals; we differ through jackknife+ conformal guarantees, molecule- and system-level difficulty normalisation, and evaluation on about 240 systems.

references.authors: Kretschmer F, Harrieder E-M, Hoffmann MA, Böcker S, Witting M
references.title: RepoRT: a comprehensive repository for small molecule retention times
references.verification: Crossref record (title match; preprint relation) and PubMed PMID 38191934 retrieved; content statistics from the Crossref record of ChemRxiv preprint v2 (10.26434/chemrxiv-2023-1mq73-v2); GitHub README checked.
references.category: Multi-system RT repository and benchmark
references.problem: No curated, machine-learning-ready RT data with chromatographic metadata existed for transferable prediction.
references.data: Preprint v2: 373 datasets, 8,809 unique compounds, 88,325 RT entries on 49 columns, with column, eluent and gradient metadata and column selectivity (HSM/Tanaka) parameters.
references.method: Curated GitHub-hosted repository with structure standardization, automated validation and a normalized column database.
references.uncertainty_method: Not applicable (data resource).
references.transfer_setting: Supports training and evaluation across many RP and HILIC systems with their metadata.
references.main_results: First comprehensive multi-system RT repository; it now underpins transferable models such as 2-step.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/michaelwitting/RepoRT; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16267767.
references.limitations: Datasets differ widely in size and metadata completeness.
references.relevance_to_study: Our training and evaluation source (about 240 RP systems with leave-source-out folds, plus HILIC tests).

references.authors: Zhang Y, Liu F, Li XQ, Gao Y, Li KC, Zhang QH
references.title: Generic and accurate prediction of retention times in liquid chromatography by post-projection calibration
references.verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 38459241 and full text PMC10923921 retrieved this session.
references.category: Calibrant-based projection with external reference calibration
references.problem: Give generic RT predictions across chromatographic methods (CMs) to support candidate annotation.
references.data: MCMRT: 343 molecules on 30 RP CMs; QSRR trained on 1,820 emerging contaminants (CM 03p); 2,935 candidates for 112 identities.
references.method: GP-regression projections (rational-quadratic kernel) fitted on 35 calibrants, plus a re-projection from a similar laboratory CM (ReICM) that calibrates the projected RTs.
references.uncertainty_method: No interval model; candidates were filtered with a heuristic threshold of twice the RMSE for each output CM.
references.transfer_setting: Public CM to local CM, with 35 external calibrants measured on both.
references.main_results: Median projection error stayed below 3.2% of elution time, yet after calibration 6-20% of true identities were still filtered out and 29-43% of false candidates accepted.
references.code_available: Yes: MATLAB code and data at github.com/Yanzi-Zhang-oss/Post-projection-calibration-of-retention-time-across-liquid-chromatography-setups.
references.limitations: Needs a second, similar reference CM and 35 calibrants, and the ±2·RMSE windows have uncontrolled coverage.
references.relevance_to_study: Direct heuristic-window baseline (±k·RMSE) and calibrant-protocol comparator for our conformal windows and decoy-elimination evaluation.

references.authors: Xue J, Wang B, Ji H, Li W
references.title: RT-Transformer: retention time prediction for metabolite annotation to assist in metabolite identification
references.verification: Crossref record, PubMed PMID 38402516 and full text PMC10914443 retrieved this session.
references.category: Pretrain/fine-tune RT prediction
references.problem: Scalable RT prediction for any chromatographic method to support metabolite annotation.
references.data: SMRT (80,038) for pretraining; fine-tuning on 41 PredRet datasets (more than 80 compounds each) and five other CMs.
references.method: Graph attention network plus 1D-Transformer; the feature extractor is frozen and the output block fine-tuned on target data.
references.uncertainty_method: None; the filtering threshold was chosen from ROC curves (relative error 4.3-5.7%).
references.transfer_setting: Transfer learning to target CMs that have tens to hundreds of training compounds.
references.main_results: SMRT MAE 27.30 s (retained molecules) or 33.41 s (all); the ROC thresholds removed 80.9-85.4% of false identities, and the mean isomer filter rate was 59.35%.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/01dadada/RT-Transformer and a Hugging Face web server (stated in paper).
references.limitations: Needs target fine-tuning data and uses global ROC-tuned thresholds without coverage control; a later study (2-step) found large accuracy drops under structure-disjoint splits.
references.relevance_to_study: State-of-the-art pretrain/fine-tune comparator, and an example of the global-threshold practice that our method replaces.

references.authors: Matyushin DD, Burov IA, Sholokhova AYu
references.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Flagging of Unreliable Predictions in Predicting Mass Spectrometry-Related Properties of Small Molecules Using Machine Learning
references.verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 39684785 and full text PMC11641629 retrieved this session.
references.category: Uncertainty estimation and flagging of unreliable RT predictions
references.problem: Predictions of RT, RI and CCS usually come without any per-molecule uncertainty.
references.data: SMRT (RT above 500 s, one RP system), NIST 17 GC retention indices (polar and non-polar) and a CCS [M+H]+ compilation.
references.method: Features from ensemble spread, similarity to the nearest training molecule (Tanimoto, cosine, Euclidean, MCS) and k-means cluster membership, fed to logistic regression or AutoML.
references.uncertainty_method: Binary classifier that predicts whether a prediction falls among the worst 15%.
references.transfer_setting: None (cross-validation within a single system).
references.main_results: ROC-AUC 0.73-0.82 across tasks (0.733 for LC RT with AutoML); error distributions were closer to exponential, sometimes Cauchy-like, than normal.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/mtshn/uncertaintychem.
references.limitations: Produces flags rather than intervals, with no coverage guarantee, on a single chromatographic system.
references.relevance_to_study: Supports our difficulty features (novelty and similarity, ensemble disagreement); the heavy-tailed errors it reports motivate distribution-free conformal windows.

references.authors: Malm L, Kruve A
references.title: Do experimental projection methods outcompete retention time prediction models in non-target screening? A case study on LC/HRMS interlaboratory comparison data
references.verification: Crossref record (title match) and full text PMC12268317 (PMID 40671565) retrieved this session.
references.category: NTS evaluation of calibrant projection versus ML prediction across interlaboratory systems
references.problem: Test whether calibrant-based projections beat ML RT predictions for NTS on real routine laboratory systems.
references.data: NORMAN interlaboratory comparison: 41 calibrants and 45 suspects measured on 37 chromatographic systems; the ML model was trained on Aalizadeh et al. RT data.
references.method: RTI conversion followed by GAM projection (mgcv, k=6) fitted on calibrants detected in both systems, compared with a Mordred-descriptor ML prediction model.
references.uncertainty_method: None beyond RMSE and 95th-percentile absolute deviations, with F-tests on RMSE.
references.transfer_setting: Source system to NTS system through the shared detected calibrants (a subset of the 41).
references.main_results: Projection RMSE was 78.1 RTI units (7.8% of the range) versus 149.0 for prediction; calibrant and suspect RMSEs correlated weakly (R² 0.30), and projections failed outside the calibrant range (9.8% of suspects).
references.code_available: Yes: data and code in the ESI.
references.limitations: Small chemical space (86 chemicals), mostly RP systems, and no interval methodology.
references.relevance_to_study: Shows that calibrant residuals poorly predict suspect errors and that mobile-phase pH and column chemistry drive transfer error, which motivates our meta-learned, system-aware difficulty normalisation.

references.authors: Li Y, Dong K, Yu D, Huang D, Liu X, Xu G, Lin X
references.title: Prediction of Retention Time by Combining Multiple Data Sets with Chromatographic Parameter Vectorization and Transfer Learning
references.verification: PubMed PMID 40747624 record and abstract retrieved by DOI this session (title match); Crossref component records also seen.
references.category: Multi-dataset, condition-aware pretraining with fine-tuning
references.problem: RT models are tied to one column and set of conditions, and data sparsity limits accuracy.
references.data: 14 RPLC and 14 HILIC datasets.
references.method: MDL-TL: joint training over several datasets, with column and conditions vectorized by word2vec and autoencoders and appended to compound representations, then fine-tuned to each target system.
references.uncertainty_method: None reported in abstract.
references.transfer_setting: Pretrained multi-dataset model fine-tuned on each target system.
references.main_results: Beat five deep-learning and four machine-learning approaches, including SMRT-based transfer, on MAE, MedAE, MRE and R² in most cases.
references.code_available: Not determined (not stated in abstract and not found in web searches).
references.limitations: Requires target fine-tuning data, and reports neither uncertainty nor a calibrant-only evaluation.
references.relevance_to_study: Concurrent evidence that encoding chromatographic parameters helps multi-system learning, as in our base score.

references.authors: Wiczling P
references.title: Bayesian multilevel modeling of retention data informed by structural similarity of analytes
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41177069 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
references.category: Bayesian hierarchical retention modelling with structural similarity
references.problem: Retention models usually treat analytes as conditionally independent given their descriptors and ignore structural similarity.
references.data: Public isocratic RP-HPLC dataset of 1,026 analytes.
references.method: Multilevel multi-output Gaussian process with matrix-normal between-analyte variability whose row covariance is a Tanimoto similarity matrix.
references.uncertainty_method: Full Bayesian posterior predictive uncertainty.
references.transfer_setting: Within one dataset across isocratic chromatographic parameters; no cross-lab or cross-system transfer.
references.main_results: Adding structural similarity improved predictive performance, especially when data for related analytes were available.
references.code_available: Not determined (paywalled; not found in web searches).
references.limitations: Single isocratic dataset; the abstract does not report whether intervals stay calibrated under cross-system shift.
references.relevance_to_study: Supports Tanimoto-based novelty as a driver of RT predictive uncertainty, a feature family in our difficulty model.

references.authors: Beck AG, Jones G, Singh A, Fine J, Shrestha R, Barrientos RC, Sherer EC, Williams KB, Regalado EL, Aggarwal P
references.title: Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Multiple Conditions as a Framework for Streamlined Retention Time Prediction to Accelerate Method Development
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41627175 abstract retrieved; ChemRxiv preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-z39t1) via Crossref; uncertainty implementation read from public repository code (train_scripts/480_uncert.py).
references.category: Condition-aware RT prediction with uncertainty
references.problem: Speed up LC method screening by predicting RTs across column chemistries and buffer pH.
references.data: MCaRT: 480 Enamine analytes under 8 conditions (C18, cyano, phenyl and Gold aQ columns, each with TFA or ammonium acetate buffer) on a 5-min gradient.
references.method: GIN graph network initialised from SMRT-trained weights, with explicit column and buffer descriptors appended.
references.uncertainty_method: Per the public code, a heteroscedastic head (learned log-variance) plus MC dropout (100 passes) splits aleatoric and epistemic variance; the abstract reports calibrated uncertainty.
references.transfer_setting: Across four column chemistries and two buffers within one lab; analytes seen on one column improve predictions on others.
references.main_results: Cross-validated R² 0.86 and MAE 15.5 s, improving to R² 0.95 and MAE 8.2 s when analytes were seen on one column chemistry.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/MSDLLCpapers/MRL-MC-Retention (code, weights, MCaRT data).
references.limitations: Single lab, one short gradient and eight conditions; the uncertainty is Gaussian and model-based without finite-sample guarantees, and the work targets method development rather than annotation or NTS.
references.relevance_to_study: Closest recent uncertainty-aware multi-condition RT model; our conformal windows add distribution-free coverage under cross-lab calibrant transfer.

references.authors: Xiong Z, Wang X, Liu J, Cong S, Yang Q, Ji H
references.title: Unified Multitask Modeling for Retention Time Prediction Across Chromatographic Conditions
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41885002 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
references.category: Multitask multi-condition RT prediction
references.problem: Condition-specific RT models fragment knowledge and scale poorly.
references.data: 28 RPLC and HILIC datasets.
references.method: Uni-RT: a unified multitask framework that learns from heterogeneous datasets together, capturing shared retention patterns and condition-specific differences.
references.uncertainty_method: None reported in abstract.
references.transfer_setting: Joint learning over the conditions represented in training; the abstract does not describe zero-shot transfer to unseen systems.
references.main_results: Higher accuracy and robustness than pooled or condition-specific models, with simpler deployment.
references.code_available: Not determined (not stated in abstract and not found in web searches).
references.limitations: Appears to need training data for each condition and provides no calibrated intervals.
references.relevance_to_study: Concurrent multi-system learner; it contrasts with our setting, where the target system offers only n≈10-50 calibrants.

references.authors: Deng J, Chen J, Wang J, Li X, Liu S, Ge L, Ying G-G, Chen C-E
references.title: Retention time prediction of emerging contaminants via transfer learning with graph neural networks
references.verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41621299 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
references.category: Transfer learning for NTS of emerging contaminants
references.problem: Predict RTs of environmental contaminants for LC-MS non-targeted analysis when standards are scarce.
references.data: Source domain METLIN-SMRT; target domain of 1,051 environmental pollutants.
references.method: Phased comparison of 5 GNN architectures, pretraining optimizers, training strategies and TL optimizers; the best was GIN3, fine-tuned with L-BFGS.
references.uncertainty_method: Applicability-domain assessment; no prediction intervals.
references.transfer_setting: SMRT to a single target environmental dataset by fine-tuning.
references.main_results: R² 0.894 versus 0.816 for the best conventional ML method, with a smaller train-test decline (8% versus 11-19%).
references.code_available: Not determined (paywalled; not found in web searches).
references.limitations: Evaluated on one target dataset with a train/test split; calibrant-only (n≈10-50) regimes and calibrated windows were not reported.
references.relevance_to_study: Environmental-NTS transfer baseline whose target-data needs exceed the calibrant-only budgets we study.

references.title: FastRet: Fast and Simple Retention Time Prediction in Liquid Chromatography
references.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
references.verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 42670875 and full text PMC13508770 retrieved this session.
references.category: Practical RT tool with model adjustment from few remeasured compounds
references.problem: Fast, simple RT prediction plus adaptation to changed chromatographic conditions in untargeted metabolomics.
references.data: In-house RP (458), RP-AXMM (436) and HILIC (388) sets, Retip HILIC (970), six modified RP conditions and 14 external datasets.
references.method: LASSO or boosted regression trees on descriptors, selective measuring (cluster medoids) to choose compounds, and an adjustment model g(x, RT_base) learned from remeasured compounds.
references.uncertainty_method: None (point predictions with cross-validated performance estimates).
references.transfer_setting: Adjustment to modified conditions from about 25 selected remeasured metabolites.
references.main_results: Adjustment with 25 metabolites reached R² 0.74-0.84 on unseen metabolites (mean gain 0.22 over from-scratch models) and outperformed published methods in low-data transfer.
references.code_available: Yes: CRAN package FastRet, github.com/spang-lab/FastRet and the web app fastret.spang-lab.de.
references.limitations: Designed for modest condition changes and gives no prediction intervals.
references.relevance_to_study: Concurrent low-calibrant transfer and calibrant-selection work that complements our calibrant-number analysis but lacks coverage-controlled windows.

references.authors: Kretschmer F, Harrieder E-M, Witting M, Böcker S
references.title: Times are changing but order matters: transferable prediction of small-molecule liquid chromatography retention times
references.verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 42823457 and full text PMC13736644 retrieved this session; public repository README read.
references.category: Transferable condition-aware retention-order index with anchor mapping
references.problem: Truly transferable RT prediction that needs no training data from the target system.
references.data: 171 curated RepoRT RP datasets, six benchmark datasets and a human fecal LC-MS/MS application.
references.method: D-MPNN GNN with a 13-dimensional condition vector (HSM and Tanaka column parameters, pH) trained by a Siamese margin-ranking loss to predict a retention order index, then mapped to RT by a monotone degree-2 polynomial (LAD outlier removal, then OLS) fitted on anchors.
references.uncertainty_method: None; only MAE ± SD over folds is reported, and the application used a fixed 0.40 min window equal to the cross-validated anchor MAE.
references.transfer_setting: No target training data; about 15-30 anchors (standards or confident library hits) on the target RP system.
references.main_results: Pair-order error rate was 4.89% (versus 5.61% without conditions); 2-step beat DeepGCN-RT and RT-Transformer on 5 of 6 datasets under structure-disjoint splits, and 15 anchors sufficed.
references.code_available: Yes: github.com/boecker-lab/2-step with model weights and a Docker image, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22093097, and a web app.
references.limitations: Point predictions only with a heuristic fixed tolerance; HILIC is excluded and anchors are assumed mostly correct.
references.relevance_to_study: Most direct prior work on our base score and monotone calibrant mapping; our novelty must rest on conformal windows, difficulty normalisation, coverage and decoy evaluation, calibrant-number requirements and HILIC.

pre_empting_work.title: Times are changing but order matters: transferable prediction of small-molecule liquid chromatography retention times (2-step)
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Components (i) and (ii): a multi-system retention-order index learned with a pairwise margin-ranking loss on RepoRT, with chromatographic-condition encoding (HSM, Tanaka, pH), followed by a monotone low-order anchor mapping with LAD outlier removal from about 15-30 anchors, evaluated with condition-disjoint folds. It does not pre-empt calibrated or conformal windows: it uses a fixed 0.40 min threshold, has no prediction intervals and excludes HILIC.

pre_empting_work.title: Probabilistic metabolite annotation using retention time prediction and meta-learned projections
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: The idea of meta-learning on other chromatographic systems so that few-calibrant (10-50) projection comes with predictive intervals, evaluated leave-one-system-out with the 95% interval score and candidate ranking. It differs from ours: the meta-learned object is a GP prior over projection functions, intervals are Gaussian without finite-sample guarantees, uncertainty depends only on the predicted RT, and only four target systems are used.

pre_empting_work.title: PredRet: Prediction of Retention Time by Direct Mapping between Multiple Chromatographic Systems
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Monotone (constrained GAM) mapping between systems, with bootstrap 99% prediction intervals used to discriminate or exclude isomers. The authors themselves call the intervals anticonservative, and the method needs compounds measured on overlapping systems.

pre_empting_work.title: Liquid-chromatography retention order prediction for metabolite identification
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Pairwise ranking (RankSVM) of retention order learned from heterogeneous multi-system public RT data for metabolite identification, which is the basis of our base-score concept. It does not encode conditions and produces no times or windows.

pre_empting_work.title: Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Multiple Conditions as a Framework for Streamlined Retention Time Prediction to Accelerate Method Development (MC-Retention)
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Any claim to be the first uncertainty-aware, condition-descriptor RT model. It uses a GNN with column and buffer descriptors, heteroscedastic variance and MC dropout, and claims calibrated uncertainty. It is single-lab with 8 conditions and model-based uncertainty, without calibrant transfer or conformal guarantees.

pre_empting_work.title: Generic and accurate prediction of retention times in liquid chromatography by post-projection calibration
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Calibrant-based (35 calibrants) cross-method transfer with candidate-filtering evaluation (TPR/TNR, true identities lost versus false candidates accepted), which overlaps our decoy-elimination evaluation. Its windows are heuristic (±2·RMSE).

pre_empting_work.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Flagging of Unreliable Predictions in Predicting Mass Spectrometry-Related Properties of Small Molecules Using Machine Learning
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: A meta-model built on similarity to training data (Tanimoto and others), ensemble spread and cluster features to predict unreliable RT predictions, which overlaps our difficulty-model feature set. It is single-system and outputs a classification, not normalised conformal intervals.

pre_empting_work.title: Do experimental projection methods outcompete retention time prediction models in non-target screening? A case study on LC/HRMS interlaboratory comparison data
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Part of our NTS framing and evaluation: calibrant-based GAM projection versus ML prediction across 37 real laboratory systems, with pH and column chemistry identified as the main drivers. It offers no interval method.

pre_empting_work.title: Generalized Calibration Across Liquid Chromatography Setups for Generic Prediction of Small-Molecule Retention Times (CALLC)
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Calibrating public-model predictions to a new setup with a modest set of calibrants (learning curves from 20-100 analytes). It gives point predictions only.

pre_empting_work.title: FastRet: Fast and Simple Retention Time Prediction in Liquid Chromatography
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Selecting calibrants (selective measuring) and adjusting models from about 25 remeasured compounds, with performance-versus-number-of-compounds curves, which partly overlaps our calibrant-number analysis. It has no intervals.

pre_empting_work.title: Reliable Molecular Retrieval from Mass Spectra Using Conformal Prediction
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Any claim that conformal prediction is new to LC-MS/MS annotation: it builds spectrum-specific conformal candidate sets, including difficulty-grouped conditional conformal, on MassSpecGym. It does not address RT windows.

pre_empting_work.title: Simulation-Supervised Foundation Models for Retention Time Prediction in High-Performance Liquid Chromatography beyond Experimental Data Coverage (FUSE-RT)
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: A multi-system RT model integrating 179 chromatographic methods, with few-shot adaptation to unseen methods and evaluation under molecule, method and joint shift. The abstract reports no calibrated windows.

pre_empting_work.title: Bayesian multilevel modeling of retention data informed by structural similarity of analytes
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Using Tanimoto structural similarity to shape predictive uncertainty in RT models (Bayesian multi-output GP). It covers a single isocratic dataset with no cross-system transfer.

pre_empting_work.title: Large Language Models Enable Training-Free Retention Time Prediction Across Chromatographic Systems (RT-ICL), NeurIPS 2026
pre_empting_work.what_it_preempts: Training-free cross-system RT prediction from LC conditions plus structurally similar reference compounds measured on the target system (calibrant-like in-context examples). No uncertainty is mentioned. UNVERIFIED: seen only on the NeurIPS virtual page, not in Crossref, PubMed or arXiv.

facts: 2-step code and models are public: GitHub boecker-lab/2-step (source code, model weights such as models/2-step0525.pt, Docker image), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22093097, and a web app at 2-step.boeckerlab.uni-jena.de (Kretschmer et al. 2026, doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03243-2; repository README).

2-step reports no prediction intervals: RT accuracy is given as MAE ± SD over cross-validation folds on gradient-normalised RT, and the fecal-sample application accepted matches within a fixed 0.40 min window equal to the cross-validated anchor MAE (doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03243-2).

2-step maps the retention order index to RT with a degree-2 polynomial: an LAD fit with non-negative coefficients (monotone), removal of anchors whose error exceeds twice the median error, then an OLS refit; 15 anchors sufficed and about 30 confidently identified compounds are recommended (doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03243-2).

2-step trained on 171 curated RepoRT RP datasets; its condition-aware ROI model reached a 4.89% pair error rate versus 5.61% without condition features, and HILIC was excluded because HILIC columns are substantially more diverse (doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03243-2).

In RepoRT, on average 93.8% of compound pairs per dataset never change order; setup-characteristic pairs (order differs from the consensus) are 1.26% of pairs, and on these the condition-aware model reached 60.5% accuracy versus 40.1% without conditions (doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03243-2).

The RepoRT preprint v2 lists 373 datasets, 8,809 unique compounds and 88,325 RT entries on 49 columns, with column selectivity parameters for transferable prediction (doi:10.26434/chemrxiv-2023-1mq73-v2; published as doi:10.1038/s41592-023-02143-z).

PredRet requires at least 10 compounds measured on both systems, fits robust monotone GAMs, and builds 99% prediction intervals by 1000-fold bootstrap; predictions whose PI is wider than 2 min or 20% of RT are discarded (Stanstrup et al. 2015, doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5b02287).
The PredRet authors state that, because of multiplicity, their PIs should be regarded as anticonservative and not used as strict filters to exclude annotations (doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5b02287).

In the SMRT paper, ROC-optimised relative-error thresholds (27.5%, 12.5%, 10%, 27.5%) for four external methods filtered out 31%, 41%, 36% and 21% of correct identities; the projection used a polynomial fitted on 50 random molecules, and the authors concluded predicted-experimental RT filtering is not robust (doi:10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7).

SMRT contains 80,038 molecules measured on one RP method; the DLM reached median relative and absolute errors of 4.6% and 35 s, and the authors note that elution order is not well conserved among HILIC methods (doi:10.1038/s41467-019-13680-7).

Retip's ±1 min windows held on average 87% (RP) and 65% (HILIC) of test true positives and 76% of validation true positives, excluding about 25% of true positives overall, while removing 68% of candidate structures (doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.9b05765).

Post-projection calibration filtered candidates with a threshold of twice the RMSE; after calibration, 6-20% of true identities were still filtered out and 29-43% of false candidates accepted, with overall filtering accuracy of 58.6-71.3% (doi:10.1038/s42004-024-01135-0).

Post-projection calibration used 35 calibrants with GP-regression projections (rational-quadratic kernel), and its median projection error was below 3.2% of elution time (doi:10.1038/s42004-024-01135-0).

García et al. meta-learned a GP prior over projection functions on other PredRet systems by minimizing leave-one-out predictive loss (leave-one-system-out) and scored 95% intervals with the interval score; with 10 calibrants the correct molecule was in the top 3 in 68% of queries (doi:10.1186/s13321-022-00613-8).

Malm & Kruve (NORMAN interlab data; 41 calibrants and 45 suspects on 37 systems): GAM projection RMSE was 78.1 RTI units (7.8% of the range) versus 149.0 for ML prediction, and calibrant and suspect RMSEs correlated only weakly (squared Pearson r 0.30) (doi:10.1039/d5an00323g).

Malm & Kruve found GAM projections unreliable outside the calibrant RT range (9.8% of suspects had no projection) and identified mobile-phase additive or pH and column chemistry as the most influential factors (doi:10.1039/d5an00323g).

Matyushin et al. found that ML errors for RT, RI and CCS are distributed closer to exponential than normal (sometimes Cauchy-like), so Gaussian SD-based uncertainty underestimates large errors; their LC-RT unreliability classifier reached ROC-AUC 0.733 (doi:10.3390/ijms252313077).

MC-Retention was trained on 480 analytes under 8 conditions (4 columns × 2 buffers); it reached R² 0.86 and MAE 15.5 s, and its public code gives uncertainty as learned log-variance plus 100-pass MC dropout, split into aleatoric and epistemic parts (doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06729; github.com/MSDLLCpapers/MRL-MC-Retention).
FastRet adjusted an RP model to six modified conditions from 25 remeasured metabolites, reaching R² 0.74-0.84 on unseen metabolites; it reports no prediction intervals (doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.6c01344).

Retention projection back-calculates each lab's gradient from 20 co-injected calibration standards; for uncharged compounds it was 22-fold more accurate than linear retention indices across lab-chosen gradients, but it needs isocratic k-vs-phi data for every compound (doi:10.1016/j.chroma.2015.07.108).

The NORMAN RTI system uses two sets of 18 calibrants (ESI+ and ESI−) selected from 2,123 compounds, with RTI scaled to 1-1000 and QSRR applicability domains to flag unreliable predictions (doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.1c02348).
Bach et al. showed that retention order is much better conserved between instruments than retention time, which allows pooled training across LC systems (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty590).

RT-Transformer chose relative-error thresholds of 5.7% and 4.3% from ROC curves, eliminating 80.89% and 85.42% of false identities; in a MoNA/MS-FINDER test, 10 of 93 correct compounds were wrongly filtered out (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae084).

An industrial GNN RT model (120 s LC-MS method) reported an asymmetric empirical window, RT − 7.12 s to RT + 9.58 s, containing over 95% of the data, an example of a fixed single-system global window (doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.5c00514).

FUSE-RT (arXiv preprint, Sep 2026) integrates RT data from 179 chromatographic methods, adapts to unseen molecules and methods with limited target data, and is evaluated under molecular, method and joint distribution shifts (arXiv:2609.07531).

Conformal prediction has been applied to LC-MS/MS spectrum-based molecular retrieval, including difficulty-grouped conditional conformal on MassSpecGym (doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.6c00727). In this session, PubMed, Crossref and arXiv searches combining conformal prediction with LC retention time returned no small-molecule RT conformal-window study (see queries_run).
